notes: This manifest records design and repository state; it does not assert that MIX-100K has passed.
A release tag without a resolved 40-character commit or an image tag without a digest is not a complete production identity.

The exact ivekit.16 amd64 Linux image was built on the controlled four-vCPU server as local image sha256:9a9e94764b710d0520a570db4ca444418239592e8e1181bd783c4589f14045ad. At 1,400 CPS it completed 42,000 of 42,000 calls with zero failures, zero remaining calls, zero retransmissions and exact Router/CDR parity. The same image completed 42,000 of 42,000 calls while the CDR sink was unreachable; Router parity remained exact, CDR delivery correctly remained zero, and five-second warning throttling reduced RustPBX output from the previous 42,008-line failure amplification to seven lines.

A controlled ivekit.15 boundary run at 1,500 CPS did not pass the strict gate: 20 calls remained active and Router/CDR counts exceeded the expected total by four. The evidence therefore establishes a 1,400-CPS signaling baseline on this shared four-vCPU host, not production capacity, RTP capacity, Cell-10K or MIX-100K completion.

The exact ivekit.18 amd64 Linux image sha256:d36c5b94a1f63dfc5c1536f7bd00d6a23e5a3eecee26e6dfc7ebf3dd95c16b22 passed separate direct-RustPBX and SIPp-through-Kamailio 60-second 1,000-CPS gates: both completed 60,000 of 60,000 calls with exact Router/CDR parity and zero failures, remaining calls, retransmissions or queue drops; the full edge path also had exact 60,000 Kamailio INVITEs and route P95/P99 of 8/19 ms. This accepts the HTTP-capacity regression gate but is not a new maximum-CPS, RTP or production-capacity claim.

The exact ivekit.19 amd64 Linux candidate image sha256:da8407a298fe782d082c1d1f0f63609e1958f6f3f04b98d70324b7ff68a288cb was built with the pinned RustPBX, rsipstack and rustrtc sources plus the locked dependency graph. Its configured RTP/RTCP socket buffers are visible at runtime. Strict 10-call packet-sequence evidence and controlled 600/800-call throughput evidence pass on the shared four-vCPU host; the 150-call strict run is generator-invalid and the 900-call throughput runs are mixed or inconclusive, so independent-generator and Cell-10K capacity remain release gates.
Business licensing decisions are outside this architecture record; engineering traceability and source identity remain release requirements.
RTPengine Goal 2 userspace implementation finalized with exact-artifact functional evidence; benchmark and capacity claim remain not_run/none.

components.name: RustPBX
components.role: SIP B2BUA, IVR, RTP proxy, recording fork, and voice interaction owner

patches.purpose: Expose bounded dialog observation needed by iveKit voice control and audit.
Add controlled originate and hangup commands used by the iveKit voice gateway.
Build against the separately pinned and patched rsipstack source tree.
Build against the separately pinned and patched rustrtc source tree.
Replace per-INVITE control-plane routing calls with signed, short-lived, tenant-fenced HMAC route snapshots and an in-memory lookup, including standards-compliant display-name SIP To parsing.
Require exact Cell and RustPBX node admission before an inbound INVITE may use the local signed route snapshot.

Embed the Rust component guard, accept standards-compliant SIP Call-ID words while keeping node IDs strict, authorize inbound ownership through the local component-node agent, and fence every tracked RWI mutation by the exact owner epoch.
Rotate bounded local encoded recording segments, publish durable owner-fenced manifests, and keep legacy HTTP/S3 upload outside iveKit spool mode.
Bind profile-tunable rsipstack transaction, queue, cache and transport limits into RustPBX and export bounded-cardinality overload telemetry.

Move recording codec and disk work out of RTP forwarding loops through profile-tunable bounded capture queues, bounded pre-finalization draining, one-shot disk-failure circuit breaking, and explicit low-cardinality drop telemetry.

Remove session teardown awaits from the media command loop, submit recording finalization first, and bound playback, MCU, and bridge cleanup with explicit concurrency, timeout, and low-cardinality outcome telemetry.
Replace the serialized linear WebPhone pre-authentication registry with O(1) keyed lookup and generation-fenced connection-lifetime cleanup.
Make the asynchronous call-record handoff bounded and profile-tunable, expose low-cardinality loss and queue telemetry, and remove per-call log amplification from the signaling path.
Keep upstream local CDR persistence enabled by default while allowing iveKit to disable the duplicate RustPBX database write when its authenticated HTTP CDR sink is authoritative.
Run call-record sinks and hooks on a bounded dedicated Tokio runtime so downstream latency cannot consume SIP transaction workers.
Count sink failures by a fixed low-cardinality stage and globally rate-limit failure warnings to one every five seconds.
Fence JWT, WebPhone pre-authentication and REGISTER identities at their protocol boundaries without applying WebPhone identity rules to authenticated SIP trunks.

Tee negotiated speech audio into a bounded non-blocking queue, decode it to mono PCM16 at 16 kHz off the RTP path, and deliver it over a framed local Unix stream authorized by a trusted per-session token propagated by dynamic or snapshot routing.
Use asynchronous DNS resolution, retain enough idle HTTP connections for the bounded CDR saver, and apply one keepalive policy to dynamic call routing and CDR delivery.

Add a bounded native media-control client with deterministic cross-language command identity, production mTLS, secret-file loading, incremental response limits, explicit before/after-transport failure semantics and safe bounded failure codes without touching RTP packet forwarding.

Bind ordinary SIP relay initial and bidirectional mid-dialog offer/answer transactions plus RTP DTMF injection to owner-fenced RTPengine reservations, retain safe media-control failure codes across the lifecycle boundary, return unsolicited RTPengine DTMF over a bounded replayable per-owner event stream, and close allocated media through a stable replayable delete bounded outside the SIP cleanup path while keeping IVR, queue, recording, audio-tap, WebRTC, parallel-fork and offerless profiles on the existing local media graph.

Commit bounded PII-minimized per-leg dialog recovery state through the cell-local mTLS shadow service before visible T1 18x, 200 and successful in-dialog responses, with exact replay after uncertain transport outcomes and ordinary-profile isolation.

Authenticate reciprocal two-leg recovery capsules, claim and consume one-time owner takeover, atomically publish the new owner epoch, restore RTPengine media state, and run a recovered B2BUA controller for in-dialog signaling, SDP renegotiation and bounded terminal cleanup.

Emit owner-fenced dual-leg CDR projections with exact route revision and recovered timing, hash-bind the configured Region before upload, persist T1 termination intent before Region commit, bind terminal repair to the exact Region receipt and durability contract, use bounded concurrent exact commits without a global network lock, finalize terminating takeovers without restoring SIP or media, and delete records only after an authenticated Region durable-quorum receipt.

Make the durable dual-leg spool the only authoritative CDR sink, preserve bounded call-record queue tuning through an explicit no-op sink, and protect replay delivery with production-required client identity and private-CA verification.

Propagate a deterministic sampled W3C trace context from each RustPBX call into cell-local media-control requests without exposing raw call identity, SDP, phone numbers, authorization material or service secrets.
Align snapshot inbound-admission parsing with the direct iveKit HTTP response body so successful Cell reservation and ownership admission can enter the local signed route snapshot.

Freeze tenant, Cell, owner node and validated media-processing codec facts per call; preserve them across takeover recovery; route RWI and SIP INFO DTMF through the authoritative media lifecycle; reconcile exact command identity; retain bounded cleanup retry; and fail processing overload closed with SIP backoff instead of local-media fallback.

Reserve asynchronous recorder startup per session, reject duplicate or overlapping lifecycle work before disk dispatch, and release start/finalization reservations on every success, failure, cancellation and bounded-queue rejection path.

Consume the durable processing terminal stream with an independent cursor, inject only exact owner- and media-reservation-fenced playback/gather completion events into the live call, and replay rather than acknowledge delivery failures.

Execute the existing IVR application through owner-fenced processing media with strict prompt and gather commands, durable terminal projection, SIP INFO digit injection, and a native single-leg commit that does not allocate or transcode toward a fake remote endpoint.

Retain each stateful 300-699 server INVITE transaction until ACK, Timer H, transport failure or shutdown without retaining the business-concurrency slot, and count abnormal terminal causes with fixed-cardinality telemetry.

implemented_changes.summary: Use an O(1) keyed WebSocket pre-authentication registry with generation-fenced connection-lifetime cleanup.

The exact ivekit.16 source compiled into the controlled amd64 Linux benchmark image and its SIP trunk path sustained the strict 1,400-CPS baseline; runtime WSS load remains not_run.

implemented_changes.summary: Bound and tune asynchronous CDR handoff, emit queue loss telemetry, rate-limit overload warnings, and remove per-call info logging.

The ivekit.16 Linux image with 64 asynchronous save tasks and a 65,536-entry queue completed 42,000 of 42,000 calls at 1,400 CPS with exact Router/CDR parity and zero queue-drop logs; the previous 256-task deployment override saturated the shared Router and is no longer the default.

implemented_changes.summary: Make duplicate local CDR persistence optional while preserving the upstream enabled-by-default behavior.

During the strict ivekit.16 1,400-CPS run PostgreSQL peak CPU remained below the earlier duplicate-write and authentication-fallthrough failure profile while CDR parity stayed exact.

implemented_changes.summary: Run all CDR saver and hook work on a dedicated bounded Tokio runtime instead of SIP transaction workers.
acceptance_evidence: Configuration, renderer, Compose and both Helm charts carry a validated 1-through-16 worker-thread setting with a default of one.
The exact ivekit.16 Linux build includes the isolated callrecord-worker runtime.
With the CDR sink unreachable, 42,000 of 42,000 calls still completed at 1,400 CPS with zero failed or remaining calls and exact Router parity.

implemented_changes.summary: Count CDR sink failures by fixed stage and rate-limit warning output under a sustained sink outage.

The sink-failure counter uses only the fixed save and hook stage values.
A 30-second 1,400-CPS CDR outage completed 42,000 calls and emitted seven rate-limited RustPBX lines instead of the previous approximately 42,008 per-record lines.

Static contracts prevent reintroducing a generic post-backend username comparison that previously caused authenticated trunks to fall through into database authentication.
The exact ivekit.16 image completed the strict 1,400-CPS authenticated inbound trunk baseline with 42,000 successful calls and exact Router/CDR parity.

implemented_changes.summary: Expose authorized per-session caller and callee speech as normalized 16 kHz PCM without adding Provider, network, storage or database work to RTP forwarding.
acceptance_evidence: The exact ivekit.17 patch queue passes cargo check --locked on the controlled amd64 Linux server.

Ten targeted Rust tests cover trusted routed-header authorization, snapshot token propagation and validation, framed binary PCM envelopes, PCMU normalization, bounded queue overflow, bounded control messages, BridgePeer forwarding and ForwardingTrack forwarding.
Both media implementations publish with try_send and continue when the audio queue is full; provider I/O is isolated behind the local Unix stream consumer.

The Node gateway verifies short-lived session-bound tokens and nonce replay over a real local Unix socket contract; cross-process RustPBX RTP capture, external Provider streaming and physical capacity remain not_run.

implemented_changes.summary: Remove blocking DNS and avoid connection churn in the dynamic route and CDR HTTP clients under sustained SIP admission.

Dynamic routing and CDR delivery share the same keepalive policy with 64 retained idle connections per host.

implemented_changes.summary: Give each RustPBX call a bounded, owner-fenced native path to the cell-local media-control service while keeping network I/O outside RTP forwarding.
acceptance_evidence: The patch applies after the exact ivekit.21 queue and compiles with the locked Rust 1.94.1 dependency graph.

Six focused Rust tests cover the TypeScript-compatible command ID golden vector, per-call sequence allocation, incremental response limits, production HTTPS enforcement, malformed deterministic responses and rejection before transport when inflight capacity is exhausted.

The client disables transparent gzip and redirects, uses one total request deadline, bounds request and response bytes, rejects symlinked or overly permissive secret files, and requires identity plus CA PEM in production.
No RTP packet, media engine or forwarding-track source is modified by this patch; SIP lifecycle wiring and real server mTLS integration remain Goal 3 follow-up work.

implemented_changes.summary: Commit ordinary relay initial and bidirectional mid-dialog offer/answer mutations plus RTP DTMF through media-control before exposing RTPengine effective SDP or call state, route unsolicited DTMF back to the owning RustPBX call channel, and close allocated media with a stable replayable delete outside the SIP critical path.
acceptance_evidence: The patch applies after the exact ivekit.22 queue and the complete ivekit.25 source passes locked Rust 1.94.1 library compilation.

Nineteen focused Rust tests cover immutable owner binding, bounded leg and branch state, explicit profile selection, offerless and late-offer state, monotonic initial and mid-dialog sequences, bidirectional SIP tag orientation including early-media cleanup, PII-free branch identity, unknown freezing, effective-SDP identity checks, cancellation without allocation and stable delete replay after an uncertain response.

Two Rust decoder tests and six TypeScript broker/HTTP tests cover bounded incremental NDJSON parsing, strict owner and sequence validation, owner takeover, replay gaps, authenticated streaming and isolation of RTPengine notifications from command promises.

Ordinary relay calls execute offer before outbound INVITE, update(answer) before caller 183 and answer before caller 200; caller/callee re-INVITE and UPDATE reuse the reservation with monotonic sequences, 491 retries are bounded, and malformed or unknown committed snapshots fail closed.

Each RustPBX node opens one media event stream, resumes from its last committed sequence and delivers DTMF through the existing bounded call command channel; media-control retains a bounded per-owner replay window and never broadcasts events across owners.

SipSession cleanup bounds media-control deletion to 250 ms, keeps the same command identity across retries, leaves uncertain deletes to durable WAL reconciliation, and never issues an identity-free network delete from Drop.

The media-control agent restores complete orphan candidates from its backward-compatible WAL and releases them only after lease expiry plus proof that both the owner and component reservation are absent; invalid timestamps and authority outages fail closed.
IVR, queue, recording, audio tap, WebRTC bridge, parallel fork, explicit bypass and offerless calls retain the local RustPBX graph; real server RTPengine, TURN and capacity validation remain not_run.

implemented_changes.summary: Persist T1 dialog recovery snapshots locally and across RustPBX fault domains before exposing state-changing SIP success while keeping ordinary calls independent of the shadow path.
acceptance_evidence: The exact patch applies after ivekit.25, seven focused Rust tests pass with Rust 1.94.1, and the complete ivekit.26 source passes locked compilation.
The Rust client uses one bounded mTLS request, secret-file authentication, exact request replay after unknown outcomes and per-dialog monotonic sequence validation.

The TypeScript coordinator fsyncs the local versioned CRC WAL, publishes deterministic Cell-scoped JetStream records, accepts only durable remote ACKs from distinct RustPBX fault domains, and proves three or five file-backed stream replicas span at least two NATS fault domains.
T1 admission fails closed when remote durable health is insufficient; VOICE-ORDINARY does not depend on the shadow service.
RustPBX commits caller and callee dialog legs before visible 180, 183, 200 and successful state-changing in-dialog responses without storing raw Call-ID, branch identity or SDP in the durable record.
Real multi-node NATS and SIP server validation remains not_run until the Goal 3 server regression gate.

implemented_changes.summary: Recover both confirmed B2BUA legs and the RTPengine reservation under one fenced owner epoch, then continue in-dialog signaling through one serialized controller.
acceptance_evidence: AES-256-GCM recovery capsules authenticate tenant, Cell, dialog, owner epoch and sequence while preserving the original interaction identity and reciprocal caller/callee relationship.
The new owner commits both legs as one hash-bound pair before consuming the one-time takeover token; uncertain consume outcomes are resolved only through the authoritative owner endpoint.

The recovered controller relays INFO, OPTIONS, NOTIFY, REFER, MESSAGE and PUBLISH, performs bidirectional re-INVITE/UPDATE through the restored RTPengine lifecycle, advances both snapshots atomically, and bounds BYE/media/owner cleanup.

Nineteen Rust recovery contract tests, four recovered-media takeover tests and the complete 247-test rsipstack library suite pass on clean fixed-source clones with Rust 1.94.1 after replaying the exact ivekit.27 queue and locked library compilation.

The standalone 402-file source context installs, compiles and verifies the packaged dialog-shadow executable; Compose and Helm static contracts require node-local mTLS, persistent WAL and fail-closed T1 activation without coupling ordinary voice to PostgreSQL or NATS.
Physical multi-node failover, real RTP continuity, three-node JetStream fault-domain loss and takeover RTO remain not_run.

implemented_changes.summary: Converge one monotonic owner-fenced CDR projection for both B2BUA legs, including route revision, winning branch, early media, transfer chain, media outcome and recovery timing, through a restart-safe local spool and authenticated Region durable-quorum receipt.
acceptance_evidence: The exact ivekit.28 patch queue applies after dialog recovery and the locked RustPBX library compiles with Rust 1.94.1.

Sixty-one focused iveKit Rust library tests, one independent missing-callee terminal test and twenty dialog-shadow contract tests pass against the exact modified source; the Task 9 file adds no Clippy warning.

The spool writer is initialized before readiness, fences only new admission on saturation, applies bounded asynchronous MPSC backpressure to existing terminal calls without blocking OS or Tokio worker threads, retains failed batches for bounded-backoff retry and acknowledges through oneshot only after file and directory durability; the uploader resumes pending local records before accepting new owner-authorized calls, bounds every scan and response, rejects redirects and insecure production endpoints, and removes a record only after validating a matching committed receipt.

TypeScript convergence tests prove both-leg preservation, monotonic sequence, exact replay, conflict detection, stale missing-leg fill, no duplicate billing event and pending-to-committed promotion only after a Region durable-quorum receipt.

New sequence admission selects only the configured local Region contract; exact historical replay returns its journaled receipt, while higher sequence Region takeover cannot reuse the previous Region contract.

Append-only submission and receipt journals bind tenant, call, sequence and payload hash through a composite PostgreSQL foreign key; unknown or changed historical payloads fail closed without duplicate billing.

T1 requires local file and directory durability followed by an exact current-Region cross-Zone committed receipt before committing the reciprocal terminal shadow pair; a failed Region commit leaves the shadow takeover-eligible and recovered owners follow the same ordering. Ordinary mode uses local durable spool as its success boundary and does not claim zero loss for simultaneous sole-spool loss plus process kill. No Rust RTP forwarding or media packet hot-path source is modified; physical Region quorum loss, process restart, cross-Zone receipt and load testing remain not_run.

implemented_changes.summary: Remove the incompatible legacy multipart CDR delivery path and protect the authoritative durable dual-leg replay path with mutually authenticated TLS.
acceptance_evidence: The patch applies after the exact dual-leg CDR patch and before media tracing on the pinned RustPBX source; the complete patch queue passes independent git apply checks.
An explicit no-op CallRecord storage variant retains bounded teardown queue and worker controls without serializing or retrying a second incompatible network representation.

Production CDR startup requires an HTTPS endpoint, a bounded client identity PEM and a bounded private CA PEM; the client disables redirects and response decompression while retaining bounded connect and request timeouts.
The OPC process exposes a separate internal TLS listener requiring a trusted client certificate while retaining the public HTTP and WebSocket listener unchanged.

Compose and both Helm deployment surfaces mount separate server and client credentials without embedding private material. Exact-source compile, image build, spool replay and PostgreSQL durable-receipt verification remain release gates for ivekit.35.

implemented_changes.summary: Propagate bounded sampled W3C trace context across RustPBX and cell-local media-control while preserving the media hot path and sensitive-data boundary.
acceptance_evidence: The patch applies after the exact ivekit.28 queue on the pinned RustPBX source; independent git apply, rustfmt and diff checks pass.
A stable SHA-256-derived trace identifier binds commands from the same call without transmitting the raw call identifier, while each command receives a separate span identifier.
Deterministic sampling is configurable from zero through one and defaults to one percent in the deployment surfaces.
The tracing patch adds no SDP, phone number, authorization token or service-secret logging, and does not modify RTP packet forwarding source.
The ivekit.35 native locked compile passes; image build, multi-Pod trace continuity and server overhead comparison remain not_run.

implemented_changes.summary: Consume the direct successful iveKit inbound-admission response without an obsolete data envelope.
acceptance_evidence: A focused patch contract test requires the exact response parser change to follow the complete ivekit.29 queue.
The parser retains accepted, route revision, owner epoch, reservation, authorization context and optional audio-tap validation while removing only the nonexistent data envelope.
Exact-source locked compilation passes as part of ivekit.35; image build and real SIPp signaling remain release gates.

implemented_changes.summary: Bind every RustPBX call to one immutable owner and media-processing profile across admission, RWI mutation, real outbound SDP negotiation, cleanup and dialog recovery.
acceptance_evidence: The exact ivekit.35 patch applies after the direct inbound-admission response contract and passes Rust 1.94.1 Rustfmt.
Seventy-six focused iveKit Rust library tests and twenty dialog-shadow contract tests pass against the exact modified source after a clean fixed-source replay.
Unknown, partial, mismatched-codec, invalid-payload-type and non-20-ms processing profiles fail before media allocation.
Inbound and outbound owner contracts carry tenant, Cell, node, route revision, availability, authorization reference and media profile; owner conflicts compare the complete immutable contract.

Processing offers carry the frozen G.711/Opus codec pair, RTP payload types and packetization interval, while recovery capsules preserve the same profile and historical capsules migrate only to the former G.711 default.

RWI originate uses the real rsipstack local tag, publishes only effective media-control SDP, commits 183/200 answers back to the local RTP track, reconciles unknown mutations by exact command identity, closes media reservation on every terminal branch, retains unconfirmed cleanup in a bounded background retry queue, and closes only an owner opened by the synchronously failed command.

implemented_changes.summary: Route processing-profile SIP INFO digits to the bound worker with stable event identity and convert capacity or retryable media failures into explicit SIP backoff without changing media engines.
acceptance_evidence: Strict SIP INFO parsing accepts one DTMF digit, derives a bounded deterministic event identifier and preserves the existing peer-forwarding behavior for non-processing calls.
Processing calls submit owner-fenced inject_dtmf commands to their immutable media reservation and never silently fall back to the local media graph.
Capacity and retryable failures retain their semantics through RustPBX and produce an immediate 503 response with Retry-After; unrelated fast-path reservations remain usable.
Focused RustPBX, rsipstack, voice-media-rs and TypeScript router tests pass locally; clean fixed-source replay, image build and real SIP/RTP overload remain release gates.

implemented_changes.summary: Make asynchronous recording startup single-writer per session and preserve reusable lifecycle state after finalization.
acceptance_evidence: The recording start reservation uses an atomic compare-and-reserve operation and rejects duplicate, active, finalizing or lock-busy sessions before dispatching disk work.
Start and finalization reservations are released on worker success, worker failure, cancellation, empty finalization and bounded lifecycle-queue rejection.
The original active double-start regression and a dedicated pending-start ownership regression pass against the exact modified source; complete clean-source replay remains a release gate.

implemented_changes.summary: Project durable processing playback and gather terminal events into the exact live RustPBX call without coupling them to the DTMF hot path.
acceptance_evidence: RustPBX consumes an authenticated bounded NDJSON terminal stream using a cursor independent from immediate DTMF delivery.
Every terminal event must match processing media mode, tenant, Cell, owner node, owner epoch, callee media reservation and live call identity before application injection.

Playback completion and interruption project to AudioComplete while gather completion projects to DtmfCollected; missing calls advance safely and channel-delivery failure replays from the prior cursor.

The patch applies after the recording lifecycle reservation patch and passes focused decoder, owner-fence, projection and exact-source replay tests; image build and real media acceptance remain release gates.

implemented_changes.summary: Run the existing RustPBX IVR application on the external processing media worker without creating a fake second RTP participant.
acceptance_evidence: A processing IVR sends an owner-fenced offer followed by an exact empty-payload commit_single_leg command and receives the caller-facing answer SDP from the processing worker.
The worker permanently suppresses the unused leg-B egress so caller RTP is consumed for DTMF and barge-in without unnecessary A-to-B transcoding or network output.

Only the existing ivr application may select single-leg processing; conference, voicemail, queue, WebRTC, recording, audio-tap and explicit-bypass flows retain their established media execution profiles.

Playback, stop, gather, SIP INFO digits and durable completion events remain command-sequenced and owner-fenced, while processing failures reject the caller instead of silently falling back to local media.

The exact modified RustPBX source passes 1911 library tests with zero failures, and the voice-media worker passes its complete local suite; clean patch replay and real SIP/RTP acceptance remain release gates.

implemented_changes.summary: Keep non-2xx server INVITE protocol ownership alive after RustPBX business processing returns while releasing business capacity before the protocol wait.

The three-node StatefulSet gives Tinode cluster routing and each local component-node sidecar the same stable ordinal identity.

The generated image build runs the PostgreSQL catalog Go tests before producing a binary and bundles DuckLake, PostgreSQL, HTTPFS and AWS extensions for offline startup.

implemented_changes.summary: Deploy a private, persistent, single-writer HOMER collector per Cell with immutable image identity and a fail-open Kamailio HEP mirror.

HOMER and PostgreSQL readiness are excluded from call admission, RustPBX readiness, and SIP transaction acknowledgements.

implemented_changes.summary: Build the exact fork and validate PostgreSQL catalog, HEP call reconstruction, protocol exclusions, read-only runtime hardening, collector outage and PostgreSQL outage on the controlled Linux server.

implemented_changes.summary: Measure same-host HEP overhead and validate isolated PostgreSQL DuckLake retention, expiration, compaction, idempotency, secret hygiene, and cleanup with source-bound evidence.
